newsitem.title: USA: Japan must boost economy, reduce regulations - official.
newsitem.headline: Japan must boost economy, reduce regulations - official.

text.p: U.S. officials said on Tuesday that overall U.S.-Japan relations are sound but Washington must push Tokyo to adopt policies to make its economy grow and reduce regulation to open markets to American companies.

"I believe we must continue to push Japan to adopt policies that favour domestic-led growth and to deregulate its economy in market opening ways," Robert Reis, an acting deputy assistant secretary of state, told a Senate Foreign Relations subcommittee.

Reis said U.S. officials have not yet fully analysed Japan's new three-year action plan on deregulation, "but our initial appraisal is that while there has been some progress in some sectors, particularly financial services and imported housing products, much remains to be done.

"I think we're going to have to look very carefully over the next couple of years to see how deregulation proceeds and I think it's in the interest of the U.S. government to push for market-opening deregulation as forcefully as we can," he said.

Reis said that although Japan's trade surplus with the United States fell to $48 billion last year from $59 billion the year before, the surplus was expected to rise this year as the weaker yen increases Japan's exports and reduces its imports.

But Reis said "our overall relationship with Japan is healthy and sound" as demonstrated by strong defence relations and Japan's role with the United States and South Korea in maintaining a freeze in North Korea's nuclear programme.

The subcommittee's chairman, Sen. Craig Thomas, R-Wyo., said it was difficult to move on to broader cooperation with Japan when trade agreements already reached "are not being lived up to." He did not elaborate.
Reis said monitoring shows that U.S. business has increased in Japan as a result of trade agreements, "so there is evidence that agreements do work."
